transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in today?

Well, my wife is the one who made the appointment. She... she finally got really scared about some things I've been experiencing. 

I keep hearing water running inside the walls. And men whispering in there, too, even when nobody else is in the house. And sometimes I'll look out and see this dark, wet patch spreading across the hallway floor. But whenever I actually go over and check it... it's completely dry. So, she wanted me to come in and see somebody about it.
When did you first start hearing the voices and seeing the wet patches?

Well, they didn't start right away. Before the house problems dragged on and I fell into this depression, I never heard voices in the walls, or saw wet patches that weren't there... or thought the neighbors were tracking me. 

None of that was happening back then. Those things only really showed up after I had already stopped caring about my usual life. They started after I was already just... feeling like a complete failure every single day.
Have the voices or wet patches ever continued during a period when you were no longer depressed?

No, not really. Like I was just saying, I haven't actually had a time where I wasn't feeling this low since it all started. The heavy feeling hasn't lifted at all. 

I just know that before the house problems dragged on and I started feeling like such a failure every day, I never had any of this—no voices, no wet patches, no worrying about the neighbors tracking me. Those things only exist now, while I'm in this state where I've stopped caring about my usual life. So, no, they haven't ever happened on their own outside of that.
Before this current period of depression, had you ever experienced another separate period when you were depressed in a similar way?

No, I haven't. I mean, I've had normal ups and downs in my life, like anyone else, but... nothing like this. I've never felt this kind of heavy, constant failure before, where I just completely shut down. This is the first time it's ever been this bad.
